title: An LRU cache
description:
A **cache** keeps a limited number of recently used items so they can be served without the slow original source. When it is full, a **least recently used** (LRU) cache evicts the item that has gone unused the longest. Real systems (web browsers, databases, CPU caches, content delivery networks) use this policy everywhere.

Build an LRU cache in which **every operation is O(1)**, by combining two structures from this milestone and the last:

- a doubly linked list (`std::list`) of entries in order of use, most recent at the front,
- a hash map (`std::unordered_map`) from each key to its node in that list.

A lookup finds the node through the map and moves it to the front with `std::list::splice`, which relinks it in O(1) without copying. Eviction removes the node at the back.

The program reads `capacity <n>` on the first line, then one command per line until the end of the input:

```
capacity 2
put a apple
put b banana
get a
put c cherry
get b
list
stats
```

prints

```
ok
ok
apple
ok (evicted b)
miss
[c, a]
hits 1, misses 1, evictions 1, size 2/2
```

**Commands** (keys and values are single words):

| Command | Effect and output |
|---|---|
| `put <key> <value>` | A new key is stored as the most recent: `ok`, or `ok (evicted <key>)` if the cache was full. An existing key gets the new value and becomes the most recent: `updated` |
| `get <key>` | The value, which becomes the most recent (a **hit**); or `miss` |
| `peek <key>` | The value without changing its recency or the statistics; or `miss` |
| `del <key>` | `deleted` or `missing` |
| `list` | The keys from most to least recent: `[c, a]`, or `[]` |
| `stats` | `hits <h>, misses <m>, evictions <e>, size <size>/<capacity>` |
| `resize <n>` | Changes the capacity, evicting least recent entries until the cache fits: `resized to <n>`, followed by ` (evicted <k1>, <k2>, ...)` in eviction order if any were evicted |
| `clear` | Removes everything (statistics stay): `cleared` |

**Mistakes**:

- A capacity (on the first line or in `resize`) must be a whole number from 1 to 1000000; otherwise print `error: capacity must be a whole number from 1 to 1000000`. If the first line is not a valid `capacity <n>`, print that error (or `error: the first line must be 'capacity <n>'` if it does not start with the word `capacity` followed by one argument) and stop.
- A known command with the wrong number of arguments prints `error: usage: <usage>`, with the usage written as `put <key> <value>`, `get <key>`, `peek <key>`, `del <key>`, `list`, `stats`, `resize <n>` or `clear`.
- Anything else prints `error: unknown command '<word>'`. Blank lines are ignored.
hints: `entries_.splice(entries_.begin(), entries_, it)` moves the node `it` points to so that it becomes the first element. Iterators to list nodes stay valid when other nodes are added, removed or spliced, which is exactly why the map can store them.
When evicting, read the back entry's key first, erase it from the map, then `pop_back`. If you pop first, the key is gone before you can erase it from the map.
requirements: An `LruCache` class with a `std::list<std::pair<std::string, std::string>>` and a `std::unordered_map<std::string, std::list<...>::iterator>`; every operation except `list` and `resize` is O(1).
Use `splice` to move an entry to the front: never erase and re-insert it.
Keep parsing (splitting the line into words, checking argument counts) separate from the cache class.
stretch: Add a time-to-live: `put <key> <value> <ttl>` gives an entry a lifetime in "ticks", a `tick` command advances time by one, and expired entries count as misses. Then implement an **LFU** cache (evict the least frequently used) in O(1), with a list of frequency buckets.
rules: Move entries to the front with std::list::splice.
Index the entries with a std::unordered_map.
